title: Government may call Parliament winter session in early December

ai.summary: Opposition parties protest the government's electoral-roll revision schedule, demanding transparency as Parliament may convene its winter session in early December.

facts.claim: Opposition parties say the government has not shared the schedule and are protesting the electoral-roll revision
facts.quote: Opposition parties say the government has not shared the schedule and are protesting the electoral-roll revision.

facts.claim: The winter session of Parliament is likely to begin in the first week of December
facts.quote: The winter session of Parliament is likely to begin in the first week of December

facts.claim: The government is keen to push through the delimitation-related Constitution amendment bill after failing to secure the required 360 votes
facts.quote: The government is keen to push through the delimitation-related Constitution amendment bill after failing to secure the required 360 votes, or a two-thirds majority, in April.

facts.claim: The proposed amendment seeks to increase the strength of the Lok Sabha from the existing 543 seats to a maximum of 850 through delimitation
facts.quote: The proposed amendment seeks to increase the strength of the Lok Sabha from the existing 543 seats to a maximum of 850 through delimitation.

facts.claim: Since October, Opposition parties have held marches, met President Droupadi Murmu and filed a petition in the Supreme Court over allegations of vote chori (theft) and mass disenfranchisement through the SIR
facts.quote: Since October, Opposition parties have held marches, met President Droupadi Murmu and filed a petition in the Supreme Court over allegations of vote chori (theft) and mass disenfranchisement through the SIR.

ai.background_note: Opposition parties have been protesting the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls since October, alleging vote theft and mass disenfranchisement, leading to marches, meetings with the President, and a Supreme Court petition.
